## Option 1: Live pod (most students)

### Step 1: Join a pod

- In Canvas, open **People → Groups**, find the mock interview pods, and **join one whose time you can make**. The day, time, and time zone are in each pod's name.
- Each pod holds **up to 4**. If one is full, pick another.
- **Join early.** The best times fill up first. After the sign-up deadline, groups are locked.

### Step 2: Meet at your pod's time

1. **Meet on Zoom, Teams, or Google Meet.** Anyone in the pod can post a link in your Canvas group. Allow about 50 minutes, or 60 for a pod of 5.
2. **Your number is your spot in the group roster, alphabetical by first name.** The first name alphabetically is Person 1, and so on. Use it in the [What's my seat?](index.qmd#who-sits-where-rotation) picker.
3. **Choose a timekeeper.** They open the [Timer](timer.qmd), set the pod size, click **Start now**, and paste the link in the call chat. Everyone opens it.
4. Run the rounds as described on the [Instructions](index.qmd) page. Panelists open the candidate's job page → **Interview room** → their own seat, and draw a new mood card each round.
5. **Cameras on**, if you can. Video interviews are a normal part of hiring now.

**Someone can't make it at the last minute?** Go ahead without them. A pod of 3 uses the **A+B Hiring Manager** seat. Your instructor will help the missing person find another pod.

## Option 2: Async video pod (if no time works)

This option is for students who can't make any of the pod times. Your instructor places you in a pod. Everything happens in that pod's Canvas group discussion, and nobody needs to be online at the same time.

Each pod member gets **one thread** where they're the candidate. On every other thread, you're on the panel. This format matches the **one-way video interviews** many employers use for first-round screens.

### How the two weeks run

| When | Candidate (your own thread) | Panelist (your podmates' threads) |
|---|---|---|
| **Days 1–3** | Start your thread, titled `Candidate: Your Name – Job Title`. Post the job link and a 2–3 sentence "cover note" on why you're applying. | Nothing yet. |
| **Days 3–5** | **Don't read the questions until you're ready to record.** | Post **one question in character** for each podmate. Use your assigned seat and a fresh mood card. |
| **Days 5–9** | Record **one video, 8–10 minutes**: your 60-second pitch, then each panelist's question, then one question for the panel. | Nothing yet. |
| **Days 9–11** | Nothing yet. | Watch the video. Reply with **one follow-up** in your seat's style, plus a short in-character answer to the candidate's question. |
| **Days 11–14** | Answer each follow-up in a short reply, either a video of 2 minutes or less or about 150 words of text. | **Drop character** and post your three debrief notes: a hired-peer moment, a hedge moment, and one thing to try. |

**Which seat do I play?** Your number is your spot in the group roster, alphabetical by first name. Use the [What's my seat?](index.qmd#who-sits-where-rotation) picker. Each round corresponds to one podmate's thread: Person 1's thread is Round 1, and so on.

**Posting your panel question**

- A 30–60 second video clip is best. Text is fine too.
- Introduce yourself in character, for example *"Hi, I'm Pat, chair of the search committee. Apologies, it's been a morning."*
- Open the candidate's job page → **Interview room** → your seat, and pick one of that seat's questions. Draw a mood card from the same page and let it shape how you ask.

**Recording your candidate video**

- Read the questions only when you're ready to record, and give yourself **about 30 seconds** to think before each answer.
- Record in one take if you can, the way you would for a real one-way interview. One restart is fine.
- Use Canvas's **Record/Upload Media** button in the reply editor, or record a Zoom meeting with just you.

**If a panelist goes quiet:** don't wait. If a podmate hasn't posted by Day 5, pick one of their seat's questions from your job page's Interview room yourself, and say which seat it came from.

:::

## Video-interview tips

- Put your camera at eye level, and look *at the camera* when you're making a key point.
- Light your face from the front with a window or lamp. Avoid light coming from behind you.
- Notes on a sticky note next to the camera are fine. Reading a script off the screen is noticeable.
- Live calls: unmute, pause for a beat, then answer, because lag can make people talk over each other.
